title: Two developers disagree
summary: Merge a conflicting branch while preserving both genuine intentions.

scenario.briefing: Main now rounds tax to the nearest unit. A feature branch changed the tax rate to 0.2. Both changes matter. Merge the branch into the feature and resolve the conflict so the result rounds and uses the new rate.

objectives.description: Merge main into the feature branch.
Keep both rounding and the new rate in the resolved file.

hints: Check out feature/tax, then run git merge main.
Git reports a conflict in src/pricing.js and inserts conflict markers.
Edit the file so the calculation uses Math.round(amount * 0.2), then git add and git commit.
git checkout feature/tax; git merge main; edit src/pricing.js; git add src/pricing.js; git commit -m "Resolve tax merge".

misconceptions.description: Resolving by discarding the other branch's intent.
misconceptions.feedback: The conflict exists because both changes are valid. Keep rounding and the new rate together.

misconceptions.description: Committing conflict markers as if they were code.
misconceptions.feedback: Conflict markers are not valid code. Remove them and write the combined result before committing.

sections.title: Branches are parallel lines of work
sections.body: A branch names a commit and moves as new commits are added. Merging combines histories. When two branches changed the same lines, Git stops and asks a person to decide the result because it cannot infer intent.

sections.title: A resolution preserves intent
sections.body: Conflict resolution is not choosing a winner. It is writing the version that satisfies both changes. Tests should run after the merge because a syntactically valid resolution can still be semantically wrong.

vocabulary.definition: A movable name pointing to a commit.
Combining the history of one branch into another.
Overlapping changes Git cannot resolve automatically.

steps.title: Merge and resolve
steps.prompt: Use the Git terminal and file editor. Merge main into feature/tax, resolve src/pricing.js by rounding amount * 0.2, stage it, and commit the resolution.
steps.explanation: The resolved function rounds the result of amount * 0.2, preserving both the rounding commit and the rate change. The merge commit records both parents.

steps.title: What did the merge preserve?

statements.label: A conflict resolution should preserve the intent of both changes when both are valid.
Conflict markers must be removed before committing.
The merged result should still be tested.
The safest resolution is always to keep your own side.

steps.explanation: Merging is about combining intent. A clean diff does not prove semantic correctness.

accessibility.summary: Git commands are text and the conflict file is editable with the keyboard. Checks are listed as text.
accessibility.keyboardNotes: Ctrl+Enter runs checks. The editor supports standard text editing and selection.
accessibility.screenReaderNotes: The command output reports branch, conflict paths, and status. Conflicts are announced with line numbers.
